code_actions.rationale: Cardiac arrest is documented as occurring on ICU day 4 with ROSC and TTM (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev_0002). Policy requires POA reflect timing; arrest was not present on admission so POA should be N.

Admitting H&P documents AKI with elevated creatinine on presentation and nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 contrast-induced AKI (History & Physical (Admitting), p.142; Nephrology Consultation, p.116;, ev_0003). Policy requires provider documentation/KDIGO evidence to validate N17.9 (pol_004); POA should be Y per admitting documentation.

Discharge documentation specifies a right popliteal DVT (right lower extremity) (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev_0004). Billed code for left-sided DVT (I82.402) is not supported. Recode to the matching right-sided DVT code (I82.401).

Patient was documented as 'Full Code' on the Patient Facesheet at admission and palliative consult documents family elected to proceed with aggressive care; no DNR documentation found (Patient Facesheet, p.4; Palliative Care Consultation, p.334; ev_0005, ev_0010). Remove Z66.

discharge_disposition: 62 - Discharged/transferred to an inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF)

evidence.quote: Assessment Acute anterior STEMI with hemodynamic collapse. TIMI 2 flow post-PCI to proximal LAD; residual multivessel disease in circumflex and RCA territories. Cardiogenic shock requiring Impella CP and IABP support.

The course was complicated by contrast-induced acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2, non-dialysis), pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with successful ROSC after 8 minutes of ACLS and targeted temperature management, and cardiogenic shock refractory to medical therapy.
KDIGO stage 2 AKI from iodinated contrast exposure in setting of cardiogenic shock and poor perfusion. Creatinine peak 2.8; oliguric with adequate response to careful diuresis.

Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses Resolved acute anterior STEMI status post primary PCI to LAD and emergency 3-vessel CABG; heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35-40%); resolved cardiogenic shock; resolved post-cardiac-arrest state with intact neurologic function; resolved post-cardiotomy atrial fibrillation; contrast-induced AKI with renal recovery; superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) on cefazolin with wound VAC; right popliteal DVT on apixaban; type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; ICU-acquired weakness.
Advance Directives & Code Status Code Status Full Code
Impella CP and intra-aortic balloon pump were placed for hemodynamic support, and the patient was intubated for pulmonary edema.
Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar.
ABG pH 7.28 / PaCO2 34 / PaO2 62 on NRB 15L.

The post-operative course was complicated by post-cardiotomy hypotension requiring transfusion, failed extubation from flash pulmonary edema with reintubation on ICU day 11, new-onset atrial fibrillation post-cardiotomy controlled with amiodarone, a superficial sternal wound infection with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus treated with cefazolin and wound VAC therapy, catheter-associated right popliteal DVT treated with therapeutic anticoagulation, and profound ICU-acquired weakness.

History / Impression of Consultant Consultation requested by the primary care team. Chart reviewed and patient examined at the bedside. Patient with severe cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest with ROSC, and pending emergency high-risk surgery. Spouse and adult children present. Family understands severity but wishes to proceed with surgical intervention.

policy_citations.section: Validation Criteria › Medical — Cardiogenic Shock without Cardiac Procedure Pathway
policy_citations.quote: 1. Criterion 1 — Provider Documentation of Cardiogenic Shock: Provider documentation (attending physician, cardiologist, or intensivist) of 'cardiogenic shock' as a confirmed clinical diagnosis in the assessment, discharge summary, or clinical note — not as a rule-out, differential, or pre-shock state. Documentation of the cardiac etiology precipitating the shock must be present.

policy_citations.document: Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx
policy_citations.quote: 1. Criterion 1 — Provider Documentation of Diagnosis: Provider documentation of acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (or acute hypoxemic respiratory failure) as a clinically confirmed diagnosis in the assessment, problem list, or plan — not as a rule-out or differential diagnosis.

policy_citations.document: Policy Documents/DRG/Cardiac Arrest with Return of Spontaneous Circulation.docx
policy_citations.section: Validation Criteria › Medical — Primary Cardiac Arrest with ROSC Pathway
policy_citations.quote: 1. Criterion 1 — Provider Documentation of Pulseless Arrest Event: Provider documentation (physician, advanced practice provider, or resuscitation team note) explicitly confirming a pulseless, unresponsive cardiac arrest event requiring active cardiopulmonary resuscitation (chest compressions, defibrillation, or both). Documentation must include the arrest setting (in-hospital vs. out-of-hospital) and must not be limited to a brief arrhythmia episode or near-syncope without pulselessness.

1. Criterion 1 — Provider Documentation: Provider documentation of acute kidney injury (AKI), acute renal failure, or acute-on-chronic kidney disease as a clinically confirmed diagnosis. Documentation of 'elevated creatinine,' 'elevated BUN,' 'acute renal insufficiency,' or 'chronic kidney disease' without an explicit acute event does not satisfy this criterion.

system_note:
MR_26 (admit 2026-10-08 → discharge/transfer 2027-02-14). Review of the medical record against the governing DRG policies shows multiple coding/POA discrepancies requiring correction. Summary of what was billed and what the record shows (key citations):
- Principal diagnosis billed: I21.09 (STEMI). Supported: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142 documents an acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock on presentation (: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_26.pdf-n9, History & Physical (Admitting), p.142). Interventional Cardiology documents primary PCI to proximal LAD and residual multivessel disease (ev_0001: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_26.pdf-n12, Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34). Discharge/Transfer Summary lists reason for admission as acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock (ev_0002: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_26.pdf-n1108, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Principal sequencing to an acute anterior STEMI is supported by documentation (principal stays I21.x). - Cardiogenic shock (R57.0, billed POA=Y, MCC): supported. Interventional note and H&P document cardiogenic shock with placement of mechanical circulatory support (Impella CP and IABP) (ev_0001: Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34). Policy requires provider documentation and either hemodynamic instability evidence or MCS placement to validate R57.0 (pol_001: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiogenic-Shock.docx-b27). The record meets those criteria (ev_0001). - Cardiac arrest (I46.9, billed POA=Y, MCC): not present on admission per the timeline. Discharge summary documents a pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with ROSC after 8 minutes and TTM (ev_0002: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Policy for I46.9 requires documentation of a pulseless arrest event and ROSC; sequencing depends on whether arrest was present on arrival or occurred during the encounter (pol_003: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiac-Arrest-with-Return-of-Spontaneous-Circulation.docx-b27). Because the arrest occurred on ICU day 4, the POA flag should be N (not present on admission), not Y as billed. - Acute kidney injury (N17.9, billed POA=N, CC): mixed timeline in the chart but provider documentation on the admitting note and nephrology consult confirm AKI related to contrast/shock. The H&P lists AKI and shows creatinine elevated on presentation (creatinine 1.4, baseline 0.9) and includes AKI on the active problem list (: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142). Nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 contrast-induced AKI with creatinine peak 2.8 and oliguria (ev_0003: Nephrology Consultation, p.116). Policy requires provider documentation of AKI and KDIGO objective evidence to validate N17.9 (pol_004: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b29). Because the admitting documentation already includes AKI and objective abnormal creatinine, the record supports AKI being present on admission (POA=Y) or at minimum documents it contemporaneously with initial presentation; the billed POA=N is not consistent with the admitting H&P evidence. (Change POA to Y is supported by and ev_0003.) - Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (J96.01, billed POA=Y, MCC): supported. H&P and interventional progress notes document severe hypoxemia (ABG PaO2 62 on NRB; SpO2 88%) and need for invasive airway/mechanical ventilation; discharge and progress notes document intubation for pulmonary edema and subsequent trach-collar tolerance (ev_0008: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142; ev_0006 & ev_0007: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Policy for J96.01 allows presumption of objective hypoxemia when invasive mechanical ventilation is initiated and attributed to respiratory failure (pol_002: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b27 and RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37). J96.01 as billed appears supported and POA=Y is reasonable. - New-onset post-operative atrial fibrillation (I48.91, billed POA=N, CC): supported as hospital-acquired. Discharge summary documents 'new-onset atrial fibrillation post-cardiotomy controlled with amiodarone' (ev_0009: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Policy requires provider documentation of new-onset post-op AF and documentation of management (pol_003: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Atrial-Fibrillation.docx-b27). POA=N is appropriate. - Procedure-related infection and MSSA (T81.4XXA, T81.89XA, B95.61 billed POA=N): supported. Discharge diagnoses and hospital course identify a superficial sternal wound infection with MSSA treated with cefazolin and wound VAC (ev_0004: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). These are hospital-acquired (POA=N) and supported by documentation. - Deep venous thrombosis (I82.402 billed = left lower extremity): discharge and transfer notes specify a right popliteal DVT on apixaban (ev_0004: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). The billed left-sided DVT (I82.402) is not supported; the correct reported location is right popliteal DVT. The billed code should be revised to the right-sided DVT code (recode I82.402 → I82.401, see code_decisions). Policy-level side/late specification issues aside, the documentation clearly identifies the DVT on the right, not left. - Do-Not-Resuscitate (Z66, billed POA=Y): unsupported. The Patient Facesheet on admission documents 'Code Status Full Code' (ev_0005: Patient Facesheet, p.4). No contemporaneous documentation supports a DNR in the chart; palliative consulted but family elected to proceed with aggressive interventions (ev_0010: Palliative Care Consultation, p.334). Remove Z66 from the coded list. Procedures (summary):
- PCI to proximal LAD, Impella CP placement, and IABP placement are documented (ev_0001: Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34; ev_0006: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). CABG 3-vessel with LIMA to LAD and SVG to OM1 and RCA is documented (ev_0002: Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037). Intubation and prolonged ventilation including trach collar tolerance are documented (ev_0006, ev_0007), which supports mechanical ventilation >96 hours (5A1D90Z). Continuous cardiac output monitoring / mixed venous monitoring documented on admission orders supports 5A1221Z (ev_0010: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142). Unresolved conflict requiring human review:
- Operative/procedure-side discrepancy for saphenous vein harvest (billing lists excision of right saphenous vein, 06BQ0ZZ, while another operative line in the chart indicates left saphenous harvest). The record contains conflicting lines flagged as ; the dataset does not include a resolved operative note we can rely on. I recommend human verification of the operative record to confirm the harvest side and correct ICD-10-PCS laterality (see hitl_question: ). Because the operative laterality cannot be resolved from the retrieved rows, this single-item ambiguity is escalated to HITL despite the overall DRG-level finding. Net action taken in this audit (claim-level):
- Finding: Billing requires correction for POA flags (I46.9 should be POA=N; N17.9 POA should be Y per admitting H&P and nephrology documentation), removal of unsupported diagnosis Z66 (Do not resuscitate), and recoding of left lower-extremity DVT (I82.402) to right-sided DVT (I82.401) per discharge documentation. All other billed diagnoses and procedures are supported by the record and applicable DRG policy criteria (citations above). Evidence relied upon (evidence IDs shown inline above): (History & Physical (Admitting), p.142), ev_0001 (Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34), ev_0002 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037), ev_0003 (Nephrology Consultation, p.116), ev_0004 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037), ev_0005 (Patient Facesheet, p.4), ev_0006 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037), ev_0007 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037), ev_0008 (History & Physical (Admitting), p.142), ev_0009 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037), ev_0010 (Palliative Care Consultation, p.334), (History & Physical (Admitting), p.434), pol_001 (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiogenic-Shock.docx-b27), pol_002 (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b27), pol_003 (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiac-Arrest-with-Return-of-Spontaneous-Circulation.docx-b27), pol_004 (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b29).
rationale_letter:
Re: DRG audit of inpatient claim MR_26 (admit 10/08/2026 – transfer 02/14/2027) Dear Billing/Medical Records Team, We completed a clinical review of the medical record and coding for the above inpatient stay. The chart documents an acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock requiring primary PCI, mechanical circulatory support (Impella CP and IABP), emergency 3-vessel CABG, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and a complicated postoperative course including targeted temperature management after a pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest, contrast-induced acute kidney injury, a superficial sternal wound infection due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, and a catheter-associated right popliteal deep venous thrombosis (transfer/ discharge summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; ev_0002, ev_0004). Finding: Based on chart review and applicable DRG policies, the claim contains coding errors that require correction. Basis for Finding (specific changes required):
1) I46.9 (Cardiac arrest) — POA indicator incorrect. The cardiac arrest is documented as occurring on ICU day 4 (p.1037) after admission (ev_0002). Per the Cardiac Arrest policy, I46.x is sequenced/POA per the documented timing; because arrest occurred during the hospitalization, POA should be N, not Y (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiac-Arrest-with-Return-of-Spontaneous-Circulation.docx-b27; pol_003). We will change POA to N. 2) N17.9 (Acute kidney failure) — POA indicator should be reviewed/changed to Y. The admitting History & Physical documents acute kidney injury with an elevated creatinine on presentation and includes AKI on the active problems (History & Physical (Admitting), p.142; ). Nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 contrast-induced AKI with creatinine peak 2.8 (Nephrology Consultation, p.116; ev_0003). Policy requires provider documentation plus KDIGO objective criteria to validate N17.9 (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b29; pol_004). Given the admitting documentation and objective labs, N17.9 should be POA=Y (present on admission) rather than POA=N. 3) I82.402 (Acute embolism and thrombosis of unspecified deep veins of left lower extremity) — side/location mismatch. The Discharge / Transfer Summary documents a right popliteal DVT on apixaban (ev_0004). The billed left-sided DVT is not supported; the code should be changed to the appropriate right-sided DVT code (recode to I82.401 per the chart) to reflect the documented right popliteal DVT. 4) Z66 (Do not resuscitate) — unsupported by the contemporaneous record. The Patient Facesheet (admit) documents Code Status: Full Code (Patient Facesheet, p.4; ev_0005) and the palliative consult documents goals-of-care discussion with family electing to proceed (Palliative Care Consultation, p.334; ev_0010). There is no contemporaneous DNR order or documentation authorizing Z66; remove Z66 from the claim. 5) Operative laterality verification (HITL): the operative record contains conflicting lines regarding the side of saphenous-vein harvest vs. the billed PCS (06BQ0ZZ = excision of right saphenous vein). This conflict was flagged in the chart. Please review and confirm the operative note/OR record to determine the correct laterality and, if needed, the correct ICD-10-PCS code for excision/harvest of the saphenous vein. Correction to the claim: the auditing team will (a) change POA for I46.9 to N, (b) change POA for N17.9 to Y, (c) recode I82.402 to the right-sided DVT code (I82.401) per the discharge summary, and (d) remove Z66. All other billed diagnoses and procedures were supported by provider documentation and applicable DRG policy criteria (e.g., cardiogenic shock, acute respiratory failure with hypoxia, mechanical ventilation >96 hours, Impella/IABP placement, CABG). Please provide the operative record/OR nursing note for verification of saphenous-vein harvest laterality so we can finalize the PCS procedure code for vein excision if a laterality-specific PCS applies. Sincerely,
Clinical Audit Team
(Documentation and policy citations: History & Physical (Admitting), p.142; Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.34; Nephrology Consultation, p.116; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1037; Patient Facesheet, p.4; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiogenic-Shock.docx-b27; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b27; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiac-Arrest-with-Return-of-Spontaneous-Circulation.docx-b27; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-b29.)
